content:
Crypto natives built DeFi.

Wall Street is starting to own it.

I've been in crypto since 2018.

Watched retail traders build DeFi protocols from zero.

Now institutions are buying governance tokens, launching Bitcoin ETFs, building treasuries.

BlackRock. Citadel. Apollo.

Most crypto natives see this as a threat to decentralization.

I see it differently.

This is necessary innovation.

The US creating a Bitcoin treasury isn't just for American citizens.

It's a signal to the entire world.

When the global leader validates an asset class, everything changes.

Custody infrastructure improves.
Regulatory clarity follows.
Barriers to entry drop.

Institutions don't move fast.

But when they move, they bring capital and legitimacy that retail can't.

Here's what I've noticed working with 137+ Web3 projects:

The protocols that attract institutional attention are the ones with real infrastructure value.

Not just governance theater.
Not just token narratives.

Actual liquidity, lending, and distribution.

I scaled Lumina Web3 to $400K/month because we understood this shift early.

Institutions need onchain rails to launch tokenized products.

DeFi is becoming that backend.

Now for the uncomfortable part.

People demonize institutions entering crypto.

I think it's a coping mechanism.

When you haven't succeeded at the level you wanted, it's easier to attack those who did.

Institutions aren't killing crypto.

They're forcing it to mature.

Cleaner economics.
Tighter governance.
Real value capture.

DeFi isn't replacing traditional finance.

It's becoming its infrastructure.

And the projects that win will be the ones institutions can actually build on.

---

Worked with brands like Polkadot, Solana, Magic Eden. Generated 18B+ views in 2025.

♻️ Repost if you think institutional adoption is progress, not betrayal.

content:
How to set a short-form video strategy you'll actually use:

ATTENTION (Start Here)

1. Your Distribution Plan

If no one sees your content, your values don't matter.

2. Volume Target

How many clips per week? How many platforms?

Name the number or you're just hoping.

3. Who Owns Distribution

One person. One metric. No committees.

DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM (Your Moat)

4. Platform You Dominate First

TikTok? Instagram? YouTube Shorts?

Pick one. Win there. Then expand.

5. Your Clipping Network

In-house team? Contractor network? Pay-per-view model?

Build what competitors can't replicate in 90 days.

6. Content Multiplier

One long-form video should become 10+ short clips.

If it doesn't, your process is broken.

EXECUTION (Making It Real)

7. Monthly View Target

Not impressions. Not reach. Views.

8. CPM Benchmark

What does attention actually cost you?

Track it or you're flying blind.

9. What Content Format Is Already Working

Double down on what's working before chasing trends.

The best strategy isn't the most sophisticated one.

It's the one that gets you 100M views while others are still perfecting their brand guidelines.

No one cares about your company values if they never see them.
